text:
Ben: Seeing a pattern in production: EU clients hit an idle connection, then failover to us-east, but the resume path doesn't dedupe and we end up charging twice. Anyone else?
Maya: :eyes: I saw alerts about duplicate token usage yesterday around 03:12 UTC. Is this the same?
Ben: Probably. Logs show client does resume->403 then reconnects to fallback region. Proxy sticky policy sometimes drops the opaque session cookie during idle.
Carla: Do you have a snippet of the headers we saw?
Ben: Yep — from proxy logs: 
```
POST /resume v1.0
x-session-id: 9f2c-...-a1
x-route-variant: eu-sticky-v2
x-proxy-opaque: abcd1234
response: 403 Forbidden (stale token)
```
Then a new websocket is opened to us-east with a fresh session id and same client id. Billing pipeline counts both tokens as active.
Dan: That sounds like two separate sessions created within the same logical client flow. Our quota meter keys by session id only, so new session increments.
Maya: We already have a resume token dedupe in the runtime but only for resume within 200ms. Could be timing gap if client waits longer during idle.
Carla: Is this just SSE or WS too?
Ben: Both. Repro steps: 1) start streaming from EU, 2) simulate idle by pausing heartbeats for ~700ms, 3) proxy kills socket, 4) client tries resume, gets 403 from shard because session was tombstoned, 5) client opens new connection to fallback region.
infra-bot: Alert: stream-duplicate-billing spike at 2026-03-19T03:12:14Z (+320% from baseline). Top affected route: chat.generate.stream (eu-west-1).
Dan: Console shows a cluster of duplicated token counters at the same minute. Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/r/dash/streaming-dup?panel=5
Maya: Quick mitigations: - increase runtime resume dedupe window to 1s - have proxy preserve opaque cookie on idle socket reset - add server-side resume-token global blacklist to ignore immediate re-creates
Carla: Preserving the cookie seems risky due to L7 proxies doing half-close. Also need to ensure we don't break sticky-route semantics that prefer local shard.
Ben: Another idea: when a resume fails with 403, return a special header X_RESUME_REJECTED: tombstoned and set Retry-After small window. Clients would then backoff and not immediately open fallback.
Dan: We can add a lightweight console UX flag to enable client-friendly retry headers for canary. Ops can flip for 1% of traffic.
Maya: Telemetry change request: tag resume-fail events with route_variant and opaque cookie hash so we can attribute duplicates to routing decisions. Right now we only log tenant+route which loses the shard context.
Carla: Agreed. Also add a billing dedupe: if two sessions start within 2s and share same client fingerprint, mark the second as provisional (not billed) until 5s. That reduces spikes but could undercount if a real parallel session starts.
Ben: Tradeoffs noted. For immediate safety I'd prefer: 1) extend dedupe window to 1s (runtime patch) 2) proxy preserve opaque cookie where possible (small proxy patch) 3) add resume-rejected header (api tweak) 4) console canary for header rollout.
Maya: I'll open 3 PRs: runtime dedupe, proxy small preservation, and resume header. Tagging Dan/Carla for review.
Dan: I'll add a grafana panel and an alert refinement to split counts by opaque hash.
Carla: Can we schedule a 1% canary tomorrow at 10:30 UTC and monitor billing/dup metric for 30m?
Ben: Sounds good. Thx folks. :thumbsup:
Maya: PRs: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/412 (dedupe) https://git.internal/r/redwood/proxy/pull/211 (cookie-preserve) https://git.internal/r/redwood/api/pull/98 (resume-header)
infra-bot: Deployment: runtime/pull/412 -> canary env at 2026-03-20T01:00Z
Ben: I'll coordinate the canary switch and post back results.
